scope: Seventeenth expansion batch: 12 controlled you exercises. Three adverbial comparison/model items contrast with three direct noun modifiers (two category examples and one shape resemblance). Three enabled-ability goals contrast with three prevented-ability goals, using the same potential verbs in both directions. This is not unrestricted discrimination among you, toori, mitai and tame, nor complete coverage of you constructions.

sources.publisher: The Japan Foundation, Minna no Kyozai
sources.section: Actual HTML of ように/よう/ような（例示・比況）: structure charts, explanation A for resemblance, B for examples and manner, C for prefacing already-known information, and the teacher note on inflection like a na-adjective. Example 7 illustrates you-ni modifying an adjective inside a larger noun phrase; examples 12 and 14 illustrate verb-clause + you-na. The separately framed inference and legacy JLPT labels are not the tested target.

sources.publisher: The Japan Foundation, Minna no Kyozai
sources.section: Actual HTML of ように（目的）: structure (1), explanations A and B, examples 1-7, and the teacher notes on plain nonpast, potential/negative and other nonvolitional predicates. The actor preparing something need not be the person benefiting. The page separately treats indirect instructions and wishes; this batch does not adopt the basic-purpose attachment description as a rule for those other uses.

Actual HTML heading ようだ〔ヤウだ〕【様だ】: inflection chart; senses 1 resemblance, 2 exemplification and 4 purpose/goal. Supplement notes distinguish you-ni suru from other functions. Simplified extraction returned the separate Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten entry; it was not misattributed to Daijisen. Both entries acknowledge the formal-noun-plus-copula analysis alongside whole-auxiliary treatment.

Potential forms, section 1: group-1 dictionary final u becomes eru. Applied to yomu, tsukau and hairu; their potential verbs take the regular nai negative. This batch does not use group-2 ra-dropping or adopt a universal register judgment about it.

authoringNotes: All scenarios are original. References support constructions and attachment, not automatic naturalness of the invented examples. Independent editorial review remains necessary.

The first six questions visibly request only ni or na after printed you. The question states whether the comparison applies to an action/property or directly modifies the named noun. This avoids rejecting a different adverbial reading solely because the same sentence can contain a noun later.

Adverbial items cover a noun-based model, an adjective comparison and a past-verb model. Noun modifiers include two actual-category examples and one figurative shape resemblance. Neither you-ni nor you-na belongs exclusively to literal examples or exclusively to metaphor. Apples can be one of the fruits actually used.

The goal questions explicitly request the supplied verb's potential form ending in ru or nai, with no added words. The same three verbs occur on both sides; kana and kanji forms are accepted. Hairu is a group-1 verb: haireru/hairenai, not the separate transitive ireru/irenai reading of the same kanji spelling.

The desired result can be positive ability or negative ability. It need not share its subject with the preparatory action; preparation may be completed or still planned. Purpose does not independently assert successful achievement. A potential or negative form before you-ni is not a universal test for the purpose reading.

The full article inventory was screened. Toori/mama can describe following a model, mitai and other formulations can express resemblance, nado can exemplify, and tame can occur in other purpose formulations. Passive or nominalized ability expressions may also be natural when the surrounding sentence is adapted. These alternatives are not globally wrong; they are outside the explicitly bounded missing spans.

The JPF source IDs were resolved from its actual grammar index at https://www.kyozai.jpf.go.jp/kyozai/grammar/text/kanalist/ja/render.do, not search-generated lesson paths. Simplified lesson fetches showed only helpfulness counters, so the real HTML structure, explanations and teacher notes were inspected.

Supplementary Bunpro you-ni/you-na, noun + no-you and purpose-you pages were also inspected. A simplified fetch of the first returned a forum comment; the actual Structure/About/Related body was checked separately. Broad claims equating all examples with a single category relation or imposing a fixed confidence ranking against mitai/sou are not adopted.

All 221 previous exercise records and their identities remain unchanged against the committed baseline. The shared article gains only two scoped subsections and a reference. One stable SRS identity per exercise, not per spelling or presentation mode.
